pose: Alternating bicycle crunch with one knee tucked and opposite elbow rotating toward it

Exercise: BICYCLE CRUNCH one representative alternating phase. Lying supine with lower back/pelvis supported on floor, shoulder blades elevated. LEFT knee bent and drawn toward torso, RIGHT leg extends diagonally forward above floor with soft knee. Rotate ribcage so RIGHT shoulder/elbow approaches LEFT bent knee, they need not touch; opposite LEFT elbow opens wide. Fingers lightly beside temples, never hands pulling behind neck. Chin softly tucked, pelvis stable. SIDE-front elevated three-quarter view makes right-elbow to left-knee diagonal unmistakable, both hands and feet visible and anatomically correct. Highlight rectus abdominis/obliques only. No equipment, no duplicated limbs, whole figure within square.

review.notes: One knee drawn inward, opposite leg extended above floor, torso rotated toward raised knee with opposite elbow nearer it. Hands lightly at temples, lower back/pelvis supported; abdominal overlay only. Does not establish alternating motion.
review.independentNotes: Independent visual review: shoulders lifted, hands lightly beside the head, one knee flexed and opposite leg extended above ground. Transitional rotated crunch pose, not a claim of elbow-to-knee contact.
